 Order

This third application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.242 of 2023 registered at Police Station Dehat, District Ashoknagar (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(B) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 20.04.2023.

First bail application was dismissed on merits by this Court vide order dated 24.07.2023 passed in MCRC No.31880/2023 and second bail application was dismissed in default vide order dated 21.12.2023 passed in MCRC No.54497/2023.

Thereafter, statement of material witnesses have been recorded Chunna @ Krishnakumar Kushwah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160675599/
1 before the trial Court.

sentences.text: A s per the case of prosecution, mother of the victim reported to PS- Dehat, Ashoknagar that on 19.04.2023 around 7:30 in the evening, her daughter aged around 6 years has gone to play in the neighbourhood.
She returned around 8 in the night and stated that she went to the house of Chunna Tau (applicant).
Chunna took her inside room and molested her.
Chunna put his finger in her private part.
She ran away and came home.
On such allegation, PS- Dehat registered FIR at Crime No.242/2023 for offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(B) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Statement of witnesses were recorded.
Applicant was arrested on 20.04.2023.
He is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted.
Trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter due to previous enmity between the neighbors.
Learned counsel referring to statement of victim (PW-1), her father (PW-2) and her mother (PW-4) submits that these material witnesses have not supported the prosecution.
Learned counsel further referring to the FSL Report submits that no semen stains were found on source material of victim or the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged 38 years.
He is labourer by profession and has a family to look after.
He is sole bread earner of the family.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and home.
There is no likelihood of his tampering with remaining evidence.
Jail incarceration on false allegation is causing hardship to the applicant and his family.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
